Why it matters: The Hugging Face hack proved that closed AI systems can block defenders at the worst possible moment. The OSAA turns that lesson into an institutional coalition — and into a lobbying argument that open models are a security asset, not just a competitive threat from China.

'Anthropic has never advocated for a ban on open-weights models,' Amodei wrote. ► China Pitches Free AI to the Developing World Against G7 Gatekeeping As G7 leaders debated who gets access to American AI, China moved in the opposite direction. Why it matters: Two competing global AI architectures are crystallizing: a US-led system where access is conditional and revocable, and a Chinese system where access is cheap and unrestricted but comes with data and governance entanglements. item.description:
The US lifted export controls on Anthropic's frontier models after an 18-day standoff, while holding off on blacklisting over 100 Chinese firms including DeepSeek. Meanwhile, India-Japan forged a new economic security pact and Kioxia shipped next-gen memory — the AI supply chain is being redrawn in real time.
► Anthropic's 18-Day Export Control Ordeal Ends — But the Precedent Is Set On June 30, the US Commerce Department lifted export controls on Anthropic's Mythos 5 and Fable 5 models, ending an 18-day suspension that had disabled the models globally for all users. Why it matters: For the first time, the US exercised export-control authority over specific AI models rather than hardware — and the two-week global shutdown demonstrated how fragile model access can be when policy decisions override commercial availability.
► US Holds Off Blacklisting DeepSeek and 100+ Chinese Firms — Diplomacy Over Security An interagency committee approved more than 100 Chinese companies — including AI startup DeepSeek and memory chipmaker CXMT — for addition to the Commerce Department's Entity List last year, but the Trump administration has held off publishing the li Why it matters: The US has a fully vetted blacklist of 100+ Chinese companies ready to publish and is choosing not to — prioritizing diplomatic de-escalation over the security agencies' recommendations.
► G7 Debates 'Trusted Partners' AI Access After Anthropic Shutdown Shocks Allies At the G7 summit in Évian-les-Bains, France, multiple member countries raised with US Commerce Secretary Lutnick the idea of a 'trusted partners' scheme that would let allied nations or companies access the most advanced US AI models, Reuters reporte Why it matters: AI model access is now a diplomatic issue at the highest level. The Anthropic shutdown demonstrated that the US can unilaterally cut off its closest allies from frontier models, and the 'trusted partners' concept — still just an idea over dinner — is the first structured attempt to create a lane for allied access.

Why it matters: The AI memory market is bifurcating: DRAM for training, NAND for inference. Kioxia's comeback from a struggling Toshiba spinoff to Japan's most valuable company shows how fast the NAND demand curve has shifted.
